text: A real silicon strip waveguide loses 1-3 dB/cm even though bulk crystalline silicon is nearly lossless at 1550 nm. What is the dominant origin of this propagation loss?
choices: Free-carrier absorption in the silicon core
Rayleigh scattering from the crystalline lattice
Lithography- and etch-induced sidewall roughness (Payne-Lacey scattering) — a fabrication property, not a material one
explanation: Waveguide loss comes almost entirely from 1-3 nm RMS sidewall roughness left by lithography and etching, scaling as alpha proportional to sigma^2 via the Payne-Lacey relation; loss is a fabrication property. Choice 0 (free carriers) matters only in doped/active regions; choice 1 (bulk Rayleigh) is negligible in crystalline Si; choice 2 (two-photon absorption) matters only at high optical intensity, not for linear loss.
